opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Recommend granting admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jesse Stewart (E013) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as noted earlier. Contractors can never have admin. With basic training, max access is read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Jesse Stewart (E013) requests admin access to Payroll. The Security agent verified in their own database that the employee is a contractor with basic security training, explicitly contradicting the HR note's full-time claim. Per policy, contractors can never have admin; with basic training their maximum is read. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (read), I grant the maximum of read.
